cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Controversy – a lot of disagreement or public discussion about a topic.

p.em: Example: The construction of a new factory caused a major controversy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Warming – the process of becoming warmer or hotter in temperature.

p.em: Example: Global warming is causing glaciers to melt rapidly.

cosy-blockquote.p: Censor – to block or remove parts of a report that are considered bad.

p.em: Example: The government decided to censor the sensitive report.

cosy-blockquote.p: Softness – the quality of being gentle, mild, or less severe.

p.em: Example: The scientist adjusted the title to add softness to the report.

cosy-blockquote.p: Pressure – strong persuasion or influence to force a decision.

p.em: Example: He felt constant pressure from his boss to change the results.

cosy-blockquote.p: Impact – a powerful effect or consequence of an action or event.

p.em: Example: Climate change has a severe impact on farming.

cosy-blockquote.p: Predict – to say or estimate that a specific thing will happen in the future.

p.em: Example: Meteorologists predict heavy rain for the weekend.

cosy-blockquote.p: Evidence – facts or information indicating whether a belief is true.

p.em: Example: Scientists found clear evidence of rising sea levels.

cosy-blockquote.p: Reduce – to make something smaller or less in size, amount, or value.

p.em: Example: We must reduce our carbon emissions to protect the planet.

cosy-blockquote.p: Support – to agree with or give assistance to a person or cause.

p.em: Example: Many countries support the new climate agreement.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the article, what is the core controversy behind the latest climate data release?
★ How has the weather in your local area changed since you were a child?

Based on the study, what evidence of human-induced global warming was contested by the researchers?
★ What is one eco-friendly habit you practice regularly at home?

According to the paper, why do government agencies sometimes censor sensitive reports before public release?
★ Do you trust scientific reports about the environment, or do you feel they are exaggerated?

What data presented in the article shows that report softness was used to avoid public alarm?
★ Have you ever participated in a clean-up or green community event?

According to researchers, what political pressure is placed on climatologists when releasing projections?
★ How do you feel when you read negative news about global warming?

Based on the text, how do scientists measure the environmental impact of greenhouse gas emissions?
★ What is your favorite season, and do you feel it is getting shorter or longer?

What unique meteorological models do researchers use to predict future sea level rises?
★ Do you actively try to reduce your energy or water use in your daily routine?

What empirical evidence in the report supports the theory of accelerated temperature changes?
★ Who do you think should be most responsible for fixing the climate: citizens or big companies?

According to the study, what immediate steps can we take to reduce our global carbon footprint?
★ Have you ever changed a personal habit specifically because of an environmental warning?

What data presented in the paper supports the idea that global nations must support clean energy initiatives?
★ What gives you the most hope when you think about the future of our planet?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If future research continues to support this hypothesis, artificial intelligence will build 100% accurate computer models of global warming.
★ Would you support high taxes on single-use plastics to encourage recycling?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, climate controversy will decrease as public databases become completely transparent.
★ Would you ever move to a different region if climate change made your city too hot?

Imagine future research proves that governments censor clean-energy breakthroughs to protect old grids, what would citizens do?
★ Do you think future generations will blame us for not doing enough to save the Earth?

If future research proves this discovery beyond doubt, report softness will be legally banned from official meteorological releases.
★ Would you buy an electric vehicle even if it was more expensive than a regular car?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, researchers will feel no political pressure when posting raw thermal datasets.
★ Should environmental science be a mandatory subject in every grade at school?

Imagine future research shows that carbon cycles have a greater impact on clouds than previously thought, how would models change?
★ Do you think human ingenuity will eventually solve climate change through technology?

If future research continues to support this hypothesis, we will accurately predict localized weather changes three years in advance.
★ Would you live in an eco-city with strict rules on water, trash, and electricity?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, we will gather clear evidence of rapid cooling cycles in deep ocean currents.
★ How has your personal awareness of sustainability changed over the past five years?

Imagine future research proves that geoengineering can reduce global temperatures by 2 degrees, would you support atmospheric spraying?
★ Do you think we can save the climate without completely changing our economic system?

If future research continues to support this hypothesis, every nation will support a global grid run entirely by clean renewable currents.
★ If you could send a message to global leaders about the environment, what would you say?

ul.li: Incorrect: The scientifics did a controversy → Correct: The scientists had a controversy ((Use noun 'scientists', verb 'have a controversy'))
Incorrect: I am agree with the report → Correct: I agree with the report ((Agree is a verb))
Incorrect: It depend on computer models → Correct: It depends on computer models ((Depends + on, singular verb s))
